Eight sessions of building, coding, and testing at the YMCA

Student ID \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_    Pair ID \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

A robot learns nothing from a guess unless we test it. In this club you will predict what a short program does, run it, record what happened, and change one thing. Your explanations matter as much as a successful robot run.

### Our working agreement

We share the keyboard and robot. We ask before starting a run. We keep hands clear of moving parts. We treat a surprising result as a reason to investigate. We leave another pair’s program and attachment ready for them.

### Our two roles

The driver edits and starts the program. The navigator reads the plan, checks the lane, and records observations. Both people suggest ideas. Swap when your mentor announces it.

### A test worth recording

Write what you changed, what you predicted, what you observed, and what you would try next. Use centimeters for travel and millimeters for distance-sensor gaps. Wheel degrees describe how far a wheel turns.

## Python recipe cards

These small examples go inside the supplied student\_recipe function unless the card says otherwise. Indentation matters. Do not paste a fragment over the complete project.

| **Idea** | **Code to read** | **Meaning** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Action | await signal("Y") | Show one letter and let the action complete |
| Pause | await pause(500) | Wait 500 milliseconds, which is half a second |
| Movement | await drive(180) | Rotate the paired wheels by 180 degrees |
| Variable | travel = 180<br>await drive(travel) | Give a value a name and use it |
| Loop | for beat in range(3):<br>    await drive(90) | Repeat the indented action three times |
| Decision | if reading &lt; threshold:<br>    await signal("M") | Act when the comparison is true |
| Function call | await deliver() | Run the named action defined elsewhere |

### Common repairs

A string needs quotation marks. A for or if line needs a colon. The lines inside a loop or condition are indented. A NameError often means a misspelled name or missing definition. A device error may mean the robot is connected to a different port. Ask your mentor before changing the support code.

### A helpful explanation

“I changed \_\_\_ because I predicted \_\_\_. The test showed \_\_\_. My next change would be \_\_\_.”
